content.raw_text: 过完新年几天后的一个傍晚，哈利、罗恩和金妮在厨房火炉边排着队准备返回霍格沃茨。魔法部安排了这个一次性的飞路网连接，好让学生能快速安全地返校。只有韦斯莱夫人为他们送行，韦斯莱先生、弗雷德、乔治、比尔和芙蓉都要上班。韦斯莱夫人在说再见时流泪了。诚然，近来一丁点儿小事都会引起她的伤感。自从圣诞节那天珀西眼镜上被泼了防风草根酱（弗雷德、乔治和金妮都有功劳），冲出家门之后，她就时不时地会哭起来。

sentences.text: 过完新年几天后的一个傍晚，哈利，罗恩和金妮在厨房火炉边排着队准备返回霍格沃茨。
sentences.translation: A few days after New Year's, one evening, Harry, Ron, and Ginny were queuing by the kitchen fireplace preparing to return to Hogwarts.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of time sequence words '过完' (after finishing), the possessive particle '的', and the verb '排着' (queueing) followed by '队' (line/queue).

sentences.text: 魔法部安排了这个一次性的飞路网连接，好让学生能快速安全地返校。
sentences.translation: The Ministry of Magic arranged this one-time flying network connection so that students could return to school quickly and safely.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of particles like '了' and '的', as well as the structure '好让' meaning 'so that'.

sentences.text: 只有韦斯莱夫人为他们送行，韦斯莱先生，弗雷德，乔治，比尔和芙蓉都要上班。
sentences.translation: Only Mrs. Weasley saw them off; Mr. Weasley, Fred, George, Bill, and Fleur all had to go to work.
sentences.explanation: The structure '只有...，...都要...' indicates that only Mrs. Weasley saw them off, while Mr. Weasley, Fred, George, Bill, and Fleur all had to go to work.

sentences.text: 韦斯莱夫人在说再见时流泪了。
sentences.translation: Madame Wesley cried when saying goodbye.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...时' is used to indicate the time when an action happens. The particle '了' is used to indicate the completion of an action.

sentences.text: 诚然，近来一丁点儿小事都会引起她的伤感。
sentences.translation: Indeed, recently even the slightest little thing can trigger her sadness.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一...都会' indicates 'even the slightest little thing can'.

sentences.text: 自从圣诞节那天珀西眼镜上被泼了防风草根酱（弗雷德，乔治和金妮都有功劳），冲出家门之后，她就时不时地会哭起来。
sentences.translation: Since Christmas Day, when Percy's glasses were splattered with anti-fog grassroot sauce (thanks to Fred, George, and Ginny), she would cry from time to time after rushing out of the house.
sentences.explanation: This sentence contains a passive construction with the character '被', indicating the action happened to Percy's glasses. The phrase '时不时' means 'from time to time', indicating the intermittent nature of her crying.

content.raw_text: “别哭，妈妈，”金妮拍着她的背说，韦斯莱夫人这时正伏在她的肩头抽泣着，“没事的……”

sentences.text: “别哭，妈妈，”金妮拍着她的背说，韦斯莱夫人这时正伏在她的肩头抽泣着，“没事的…
sentences.translation: Don't cry, Mom,
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a complex structure with multiple characters expressing emotions and actions. The use of quotation marks indicates direct speech. The possessive particle '的' is used to show possession.
The sentence contains ellipsis and quotation marks, indicating that there is omitted content within a quoted text.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks in Chinese text.

content.raw_text: “就是，别为我们担心，”罗恩说道，让母亲在他面颊上印下一个湿漉漉的吻，“也别为珀西担心，他是这么个蠢猪，不是什么损失，是不是？”

sentences.text: “就是，别为我们担心，”罗恩说道，让母亲在他面颊上印下一个湿漉漉的吻，也别为珀西担心，他是这么个蠢猪，不是什么损失，是不是？
sentences.translation: Just don't worry about us,
sentences.explanation: The sentence includes the structure 别...担心, which means 'don't worry about...'. The word '蠢猪' (stupid pig) is used as an insult in this context.

sentences.text: 韦斯莱夫人搂住哈利，抽泣得更厉害了。
sentences.translation: Madam Weasley hugged Harry, sobbing even harder.
sentences.explanation: The structure '得更...了' is used to indicate that the action (sobbing) becomes more intense or severe.

indicating completion or change of state

content.raw_text: “答应我要照顾好自己……别惹麻烦……”

sentences.text: “答应我要照顾好自己…
sentences.translation: Promise me to take good care of yourself...
sentences.explanation: The structure '要...好' is used to indicate taking good care of oneself in this context.
The sentence contains an ellipsis mark, which indicates that there is more text that has been omitted or left out.

sentences.text: 别惹麻烦…
sentences.translation: Don't cause trouble...
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple command advising someone not to cause trouble. The ellipsis at the end indicates a trailing off or unfinished thought.
The sentence contains an ellipsis mark, indicating that there is more to come or something has been omitted.

content.raw_text: “我一直是这样的，韦斯莱夫人，”哈利说道，“我喜欢安静的生活，你知道。”

sentences.text: “我一直是这样的，韦斯莱夫人，”哈利说道，我喜欢安静的生活，你知道。
sentences.translation: I have always been like this, Mrs. Weasley,
sentences.explanation: The structure '这样的' means 'like this' or 'this way'. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or description. The phrase '说道' is a formal way to say 'said'.
The sentence contains a closing quotation mark and an ellipsis, indicating a continuation or omission of text.

content.raw_text: 她含着眼泪笑了，退到了后面。

sentences.text: 她含着眼泪笑了，退到了后面。
sentences.translation: She smiled with tears in her eyes and stepped back.
sentences.explanation: The structure '含着' indicates that tears were present while she smiled. The use of '后面' emphasizes that she stepped back to the back area.

content.raw_text: “那么，要好好的，你们每一个……”

sentences.text: “那么，要好好的，你们每一个…
sentences.translation: So, to be good, each one of you...
sentences.explanation: The structure '要好好的' means 'to be good' or 'to behave well'. The phrase '你们每一个' emphasizes 'each one of you'.
This sentence contains an ellipsis, which indicates that there is more to come or something has been omitted.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks to note in Chinese text.

content.raw_text: 哈利走进碧绿的炉火，喊了一声“霍格沃茨！”最后瞥了一眼韦斯莱家的厨房和韦斯莱夫人的泪容，就被火焰包围了。在高速旋转中他模糊地看见一些巫师的房间，都是没等看清就一闪而过了。然后他转得慢下来，端端正正地停在麦格教授的壁炉里。他爬出来时，正在工作的教授几乎连头都没抬。

sentences.text: 哈利走进碧绿的炉火，喊了一声“霍格沃茨！
sentences.translation: Harry walked into the emerald fire and shouted, 'Hogwarts!'
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a possessive particle '的' to indicate 'emerald fire' and uses the structure '喊了一声' to express 'shouted'.

sentences.text: ”最后瞥了一眼韦斯莱家的厨房和韦斯莱夫人的泪容，就被火焰包围了。
sentences.translation: Finally glanced at the Weasley's kitchen and Mrs. Weasley's tearful face, then was surrounded by flames.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the passive voice structure in Chinese, where the subject is acted upon by the flames ('被' + verb). The use of '了' after verbs indicates a completed action.

sentences.text: 在高速旋转中他模糊地看见一些巫师的房间，都是没等看清就一闪而过了。
sentences.translation: In the high-speed rotation, he vaguely saw some wizard rooms, all of which flashed past before he could see them clearly.
sentences.explanation: The structure '没等...就' indicates that something happens before another action is completed. In this sentence, it means the rooms flashed past before he could see them clearly.

sentences.text: 然后他转得慢下来，端端正正地停在麦格教授的壁炉里。
sentences.translation: Then he slowed down, and stopped neatly in Professor McGonagall's fireplace.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of adverbial qualification with '得' and the reduplication of adjectives '端端正正' to emphasize the neatness of the action.

words.definition: used to link a verb to a complement
used before a verb to indicate adverbial qualification

sentences.text: 他爬出来时，正在工作的教授几乎连头都没抬。
sentences.translation: When he climbed out, the professor who was working hardly even raised his head.
sentences.explanation: The structure '几乎连...都没' emphasizes that the professor did not even raise his head, highlighting the lack of attention given to the person climbing out.

content.raw_text: “晚上好，波特。别把地毯搞上太多的灰。”

sentences.text: “晚上好，波特。
sentences.translation: Good evening, Potter.
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple greeting, 'Good evening, Potter.' The word '好' can also mean 'well' depending on the context.

sentences.text: 别把地毯搞上太多的灰。
sentences.translation: Don't get too much dust on the carpet.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure '把...搞上' is a common way in Chinese to express putting something onto something else.

words.definition: particle marking the following noun as the object

sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks to indicate the structure of the text.

content.raw_text: “没有，教授。”

sentences.text: “没有，教授。
sentences.translation: No, professor.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is straightforward, with the word order being subject + verb. The word '没有' means 'no' in this context, and it is used to negate the statement. '教授' means 'professor' in Chinese.
The sentence contains a closing quotation mark and an ellipsis, indicating a continuation or omission of text.

content.raw_text: 哈利戴正眼镜，抹平头发，罗恩也旋转着出现了。金妮到了之后，三人一起走出麦格教授的办公室，朝格兰芬多塔楼走去。哈利望了望走廊窗户外面，太阳已经落到地平线上，场地上的积雪比陋居花园里还要深。远处可以看到海格在他的小屋前喂巴克比克。

sentences.text: 哈利戴正眼镜，抹平头发，罗恩也旋转着出现了。
sentences.translation: Harry wore glasses, smoothed his hair, and Ron also appeared spinning.
sentences.explanation: The structure '...着出现了' indicates that an action is in progress ('旋转着' - spinning) and has been completed ('出现了' - appeared).

sentences.text: 金妮到了之后，三人一起走出麦格教授的办公室，朝格兰芬多塔楼走去。
sentences.translation: After Ginny arrived, the three of them walked out of Professor McGonagall's office and headed towards Gryffindor Tower.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces characters moving from one location to another. Pay attention to the use of directional words like 朝 (towards) and the possessive particle 的 (of) to indicate ownership.

sentences.text: 哈利望了望走廊窗户外面，太阳已经落到地平线上场的积雪比陋居花园里还要深。
sentences.translation: Harry looked out the corridor window. The sun had already set on the horizon, and the snow on the grounds was deeper than in the shabby garden.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes Harry looking out the corridor window and noticing that the sun has already set, with the snow on the grounds deeper than in the shabby garden.

sentences.text: 远处可以看到海格在他的小屋前喂巴克比克。
sentences.translation: From a distance, you can see Hagrid feeding Buckbeak in front of his hut.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...前' means 'in front of'. The name '巴克比克' refers to the creature Buckbeak.

content.raw_text: “一文不值。”罗恩走到胖夫人跟前，自信地说。胖夫人看上去比平时更加苍白，听到他的大嗓门后畏缩了一下。

sentences.text: “一文不值。
sentences.translation: Worthless.
sentences.explanation: The sentence uses the structure '一...不值' to express that something is worthless or of no value.

sentences.text: ”罗恩走到胖夫人跟前，自信地说。
sentences.translation: Ron walked up to the Fat Lady confidently.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is quite straightforward, with the only potential difficulty being the term '胖夫人' which refers to a specific character known as the 'Fat Lady' in the context of the story.

sentences.text: 胖夫人看上去比平时更加苍白，听到他的大嗓门后畏缩了一下。
sentences.translation: Madame Pang looked even paler than usual, and shrank back a bit upon hearing his loud voice.
sentences.explanation: The structure '比...更加' is used to express a comparison, where '更加' means 'even more'. The word '畏缩' is a literary term meaning 'to shrink back in fear or apprehension'.

sentences.text: “不对。
sentences.translation: No.
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple denial, stating 'No.' The word '不' is used to negate the following word '对', which means 'correct' or 'right'.

sentences.text: ”她说。
sentences.translation: She said.
sentences.explanation: This sentence is a simple statement where a female character is speaking.

content.raw_text: “什么，‘不对’？”

sentences.text: “什么，‘不对’？
sentences.translation: What, 'incorrect'?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a question expressing surprise or disbelief.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks to indicate the structure and tone of the text.

sentences.text: “换口令了。
sentences.translation: Changed the password.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. The particle '了' is used to indicate the completion of an action in this context.

sentences.text: 请不要嚷嚷。
sentences.translation: Please do not shout.
sentences.explanation: The structure '请不要' is a polite way to ask someone not to do something.
The sentence consists of opening and closing quotation marks.

sentences.text: “可是我们离校了，怎么知道——
sentences.translation: But we left school, how do we know—
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure involves a rhetorical question using 怎么 (how) to express doubt or uncertainty.
This sentence only consists of punctuation marks, with a quotation mark and an ellipsis, indicating a pause or omission in the text.

content.raw_text: “哈利！金妮！”

sentences.text: “哈利！
sentences.translation: Harry!
sentences.explanation: This sentence is a simple exclamation calling out the name 'Harry'. The exclamation mark emphasizes the speaker's emotion or urgency.

sentences.text: 金妮！
sentences.translation: Ginny!
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a direct address to someone named Ginny, using an exclamation mark to convey excitement or emphasis.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks to note in Chinese text.

content.raw_text: 赫敏朝他们奔了过来，脸红通通的，穿着斗篷，戴着帽子和手套。

sentences.text: 赫敏朝他们奔了过来，脸红通通的，穿着斗篷，戴着帽子和手套。
sentences.translation: Hermione ran towards them, her face all red, wearing a cloak, hat, and gloves.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of adjectival phrases in Chinese, where descriptive words come before the noun they modify. It also demonstrates the structure of listing items using '和' (and) in a series.

content.raw_text: “我两小时前回来的。刚才去看了海格和巴克——我是说蔫翼。”她上气不接下气地说，“你们圣诞节过得好吗？”

sentences.text: “我两小时前回来的。
sentences.translation: I came back two hours ago.
sentences.explanation: The tricky part here is the use of the word '前' (ago) after the word '小时' (hour) to indicate the time when the action happened.

sentences.text: 刚才去看了海格和巴克——
sentences.translation: Just now went to see Hagrid and Buckbeak ——
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese places the time element before the action, which may be different from English word order.

sentences.text: 我是说蔫翼。
sentences.translation: I mean Nian Yi.
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple statement where the speaker is clarifying that they are referring to someone named Nian Yi.

sentences.text: ”她上气不接下气地说，“你们圣诞节过得好吗？
sentences.translation: She gasped for breath and said, "Did you have a good Christmas?"
sentences.explanation: The structure 上气不接下气 is an idiomatic expression meaning gasping for breath.

sentences.text: “嗯，”罗恩马上说，事儿挺多的，鲁弗斯·斯克林杰——
sentences.translation: Well,
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Adverb + Verb + Objects. The use of particles like 的 in this context is to emphasize the preceding word. The name Rufus Scrimgeour is presented in a formal and respectful manner using the middle dot · and the em dash ——.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks to note in Chinese text.

sentences.text: 口令，戒酒。
sentences.translation: Command, abstain from alcohol.

sentences.translation: Madame Pang weakly said, turned her body, revealing the portrait hole.

sentences.explanation: The structure 怎么了 is commonly used to ask what is wrong or what happened to someone.

sentences.text: ”赫敏翻了翻眼睛，带头走进了拥挤的公共休息室，“她跟她的朋友维奥莱特把魔咒课教室走廊旁那幅画着几个醉修士的图里的酒全喝光了。
sentences.translation: Hermione rolled her eyes and led the way into the crowded public lounge. She and her friend Violet had drunk all the wine in the picture of several drunken monks next to the corridor of the Charms classroom.
sentences.explanation: This sentence contains possessive particles (的) to indicate possession or relationship, as well as particles like 了 to indicate completion of an action. The measure word 幅 is used for paintings, and 把 is a particle that marks the object of a verb.

words.definition: particle marking the object of a verb
particle indicating continuous or resultative action

sentences.text: 总之…
sentences.translation: In short...

sentences.translation: She dug around in her pocket for a while and pulled out a scroll of parchment with Dumbledore's handwriting on it.

sentences.text: 我们坐下来吧——
sentences.translation: Let's sit down —

sentences.translation: A few hours after Sklinje was appointed, we met, and he asked me to arrange a meeting with you —
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is straightforward, but pay attention to the use of the passive marker '被' and the request verb '要求' in this context.

words.definition: to have a meeting; to talk face to face

sentences.explanation: The sentence is enclosed in quotation marks, indicating it is a direct quote or specific text being referenced.

content.raw_text: “你们就为这个发生争执？”哈利脱口而出，“《预言家日报》上登了。”

sentences.text: “你们就为这个发生争执？
sentences.translation: Are you arguing about this?
sentences.explanation: The structure '就为' together can be translated as 'arguing about' in this context.

sentences.text: ”哈利脱口而出，“《预言家日报》上登了。
sentences.translation: Harry blurted out, 'The Daily Prophet published it.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object, with the verb '登' (publish) indicating the action of publishing something on '《预言家日报》' (The Daily Prophet). The particle '了' is used to indicate the completion of the action.
The sentence consists of two quotation marks, indicating the beginning and end of a quote.

content.raw_text: “《预言家日报》的确偶尔会报道一些真相，”邓布利多说，“虽然可能是无意的。对，我们就是为此发生了争执。看来鲁弗斯终于还是设法堵到了你。”

sentences.text: “《预言家日报》的确偶尔会报道一些真相，”邓布利多说虽然可能是无意。
sentences.translation: The Daily Prophet does occasionally report some truths,
sentences.explanation: This sentence contains a complex structure with the pattern '虽然...，但是...' meaning 'although...but...' The word '报道' means 'to report' in this context.

sentences.text: 对，我们就是为此发生了争执。
sentences.translation: Yes, we had a dispute because of this.
sentences.explanation: The structure '就是为此' emphasizes the reason for the dispute, indicating a direct cause and effect relationship.

sentences.text: 看来鲁弗斯终于还是设法堵到了你。
sentences.translation: It seems Rufus finally managed to catch up with you.
sentences.explanation: The structure '看来...终于...还是...' indicates a sequence of events leading to the outcome. '设法' is a verb that means 'to manage to do something'. '堵到' in this context means 'to catch up with someone'.

words.definition: manage to do; find a way to do

sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks in Chinese writing.

content.raw_text: “他指责我‘彻头彻尾是邓布利多的人’。”

sentences.text: “他指责我‘彻头彻尾是邓布利多的人’。
sentences.translation: He accused me of being 'completely Dumbledore's person'.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '彻头彻尾' means 'completely' in this context. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or association between '邓布利多' (Dumbledore) and '人' (person).
The sentence contains opening and closing quotation marks.

content.raw_text: “他真无礼。”

sentences.text: “他真无礼。
sentences.translation: He is really rude.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Adverb + Adjective.
The sentence consists of opening and closing quotation marks.

sentences.text: “我说我是的。
sentences.translation: I said I am.
sentences.explanation: The structure '我说我是' is a common way to express 'I said I am' in Chinese. The particle '的' at the end of the sentence emphasizes the statement.
The sentence is enclosed in quotation marks, indicating that it is a direct quote or a specific reference.

content.raw_text: 邓布利多张嘴想说话，但又闭上了。在哈利的身后，凤凰福克斯发出一声轻柔、悦耳的低鸣。哈利突然发现邓布利多那双明亮的蓝眼睛有些湿润，他大为窘迫，忙低头看着自己的膝盖。但邓布利多说话时，声音却相当平静。

sentences.text: 邓布利多张嘴想说话，但又闭上了。
sentences.translation: Dumbledore opened his mouth to speak, but then closed it again.
sentences.explanation: The structure '想说话' means 'to want to speak'. The repetition of '但又' emphasizes the action of closing the mouth again.

sentences.text: 在哈利的身后，凤凰福克斯发出一声轻柔，悦耳的低鸣。
sentences.translation: Behind Harry, the phoenix Fawkes let out a soft, pleasant low cry.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of possessive particle '的' and the structure of describing a sound with adjectives before the verb.

sentences.text: 哈利突然发现邓布利多那双明亮的蓝眼睛有些湿润，他大为窘迫，忙低头看着自己的膝盖。
sentences.translation: Harry suddenly noticed that Dumbledore's bright blue eyes were a bit moist, feeling very embarrassed, he quickly lowered his head to look at his knees.
sentences.explanation: This sentence contains a possessive particle '的' to indicate possession, and the structure '忙 + verb' to express doing something quickly.

sentences.text: 但邓布利多说话时，声音却相当平静。
sentences.translation: But Dumbledore's voice was quite calm when he spoke.
sentences.explanation: The structure '但...时' is used to express 'but when'. The word '却' is used to emphasize the contrast between the calm voice and the situation.

content.raw_text: “我很感动，哈利。”

sentences.text: “我很感动，哈利。
sentences.translation: I am very touched, Harry.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is straightforward, with the subject '我' (I) followed by the adverb '很' (very) and the verb '感动' (touched). The comma '，' is used to separate the clauses, and the proper noun '哈利' (Harry) is the recipient of the speaker's emotions.
The sentence consists of opening and closing quotation marks.

content.raw_text: “斯克林杰想知道你不在霍格沃茨的时候会去哪儿。”哈利仍然盯着膝盖。

sentences.text: “斯克林杰想知道你不在霍格沃茨的时候会去哪儿。
sentences.translation: Skrinje wants to know where you will go when you are not at Hogwarts.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object, which is different from English. Also, the use of 会 (will) in this context indicates a future action.

sentences.text: ”哈利仍然盯着膝盖。
sentences.translation: Harry still stared at his knees.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + 仍然 + Verb + Object. The verb 盯着 is followed by the object 膝盖, indicating the action of staring at the knees.

content.raw_text: “是啊，他很爱打听这个。”邓布利多的声音愉快起来，哈利感到可以抬头了。“他甚至企图盯我的梢，真是有趣。他派德力士跟踪我，这可不大好，我已经被迫对德力士用过魔咒，非常遗憾地又用了一次。”

sentences.text: “是啊，他很爱打听这个。
sentences.translation: Yes, he loves to inquire about this.
sentences.explanation: The structure '很爱' is a common way to express 'loves' in Chinese. '打听' means 'to inquire about' or 'to ask around'.

sentences.text: ”邓布利多的声音愉快起来，哈利感到可以抬头了。
sentences.translation: Dumbledore's voice became cheerful, Harry felt he could lift his head.
sentences.explanation: The structure '可以 + verb' is used to express the ability or permission to do something.

words.definition: indicating a change in state or action

sentences.text: “他甚至企图盯我的梢，真是有趣。
sentences.translation: He even tried to follow me, which is interesting.
sentences.explanation: The structure '甚至...，真是...' is used to express surprise or emphasis, similar to 'even...which is'. The word '梢' is used metaphorically to mean 'to follow someone'.

sentences.text: 他派德力士跟踪我，这可不大好，我已经被迫对德力士用过魔咒，非常遗憾地又用了一次。
sentences.translation: He sent Delicis to track me, which is not good. I have already used a spell on Delicis, and regretfully used it again.
sentences.explanation: The sentence involves the use of passive voice ('被') and the repetition of the verb '用' (use) to indicate multiple instances of using a spell on Delicis.
The sentence contains quotation marks at the beginning and end.

content.raw_text: “所以他们还不知道你去哪儿？”哈利问，希望就这个他很好奇的问题获得更多信息，但邓布利多只是从半月形的眼镜片上方望着他笑了笑。

sentences.text: “所以他们还不知道你去哪儿？
sentences.translation: So they still don't know where you went?
sentences.explanation: The structure '还不知道' means 'still don't know' in this context. The use of '哪儿' instead of '哪里' is a colloquial way of saying 'where' in Chinese.

sentences.text: ”哈利问，希望就这个他很好奇的问题获得更多信息，但邓布利多只是从半月形的眼镜片上方望着他笑了笑。
sentences.translation: Harry asked, hoping to get more information on this question he was very curious about, but Dumbledore just smiled at him from above the half-moon shaped glasses.
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a complex structure with multiple clauses and descriptive phrases. The use of '就' in '希望就这个' indicates the hope or expectation regarding a specific question. The repetition of '笑了笑' adds emphasis to Dumbledore's action of smiling.

content.raw_text: “是啊，他们不知道，现在告诉你也还为时过早。现在，我建议我们继续上课，除非有别的事——？”

sentences.text: “是啊，他们不知道，现在告诉你也还为时过早。
sentences.translation: Yes, they don't know, it's still too early to tell you now.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '为时过早' is an idiom meaning 'too early to do something'. It's a common expression in Chinese to indicate that it's premature to do a certain action.

words.definition: exclamatory particle indicating realization or agreement

sentences.text: 现在，我建议我们继续上课，除非有别的事——
sentences.translation: Now, I suggest we continue the class, unless there is something else—
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is straightforward, with the word '除非' (unless) introducing a conditional clause.
The sentence consists of a single question mark, indicating an interrogative sentence.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks to note in Chinese text.

content.raw_text: “有，先生，”哈利说，“是关于马尔福和斯内普的。”

sentences.text: “有，先生，”哈利说，是关于马尔福和斯内普的。
sentences.translation: Yes, sir,
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows the pattern 'Subject + Verb + Object'. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or association.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important for indicating the structure and tone of the text.

content.raw_text: “斯内普教授，哈利。”

sentences.text: “斯内普教授，哈利。
sentences.translation: Professor Snape, Harry.
sentences.explanation: In Chinese, names are often written with the family name first followed by the given name. In this sentence, it addresses Professor Snape and Harry.

sentences.translation: The memory of chaos.
sentences.explanation: The tricky part here is the possessive particle 的, which indicates that 混沌 (chaos) possesses 记忆 (memory), resulting in 'The memory of chaos.'

content.raw_text: “是的，先生。我听到他们在斯拉格霍恩教授的晚会上……嗯，实际上我跟踪了他们……”

sentences.text: “是的，先生。
sentences.translation: Yes, sir.
sentences.explanation: The structure '是的' is a common way to affirm or agree with something in Chinese. The term '先生' is a polite way to address a man.

sentences.text: 我听到他们在斯拉格霍恩教授的晚会上…
sentences.translation: I heard them at Professor Slaghoorn's evening party...
sentences.explanation: This sentence follows the typical Subject-Verb-Object structure in Chinese. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or association between '教授' (professor) and '晚会' (evening party).
This sentence contains an ellipsis, indicating that there is more information to come or that something has been omitted.

sentences.text: 嗯，实际上我跟踪了他们…
sentences.translation: Hmm, actually I tracked them...
sentences.explanation: The particle '了' in this context indicates the completion of the action of tracking.

sentences.translation: The memories of chaos.
sentences.explanation: The structure '混沌的' indicates possession, similar to 'of chaos' in English.
The sentence ends with a quotation mark followed by an ellipsis, indicating a pause or continuation in the text.

content.raw_text: 邓布利多不动声色地听着。哈利讲完后他沉默了一会儿，然后说道：“谢谢你告诉我，哈利，但我建议你别把它放在心上。我认为这不是很重要。”

sentences.text: 邓布利多不动声色地听着。
sentences.translation: Dumbledore listened quietly.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Adverb + Verb + Object. The adverbial marker '地' is used to modify the verb '听' (listen).

sentences.text: 哈利讲完后他沉默了一会儿，然后说道：“谢谢你告诉我，哈利，但我建议你别把它放在心上。
sentences.translation: After Harry finished speaking, he fell silent for a moment, then said, 'Thank you for telling me, Harry, but I suggest you not to take it to heart.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a polite way of declining a suggestion or advice, common in Chinese culture. The structure '建议你别' means 'I suggest you not to.'

sentences.text: 我认为这不是很重要。
sentences.translation: I think this is not very important.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不是' is used to form a negative sentence in Chinese, where '不' means 'not' and '是' means 'is/be'.
This sentence only contains a closing quotation mark and a space, with no actual text content.

sentences.text: “不是很重要？
sentences.translation: Not very important?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is different from English, where the question mark comes at the end of the sentence. The use of "很" (very) before "重要" (important) is a common way to emphasize the degree of importance in Chinese.

sentences.text: ”哈利不相信地说，“教授，你理解——
sentences.translation: Harry said incredulously, "Professor, you understand—
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + 不 + Verb + 地 + Verb + ， indicating disbelief or doubt in Harry's statement. The em dash (——) is used to indicate a pause or interruption in speech.
The sentence consists of a single question mark, indicating a question or uncertainty.
The sentence is empty, consisting only of a closing quotation mark and a space. This may indicate a pause or a break in the text.

content.raw_text: “是的，哈利，感谢上天赐予我非凡的智力，我理解你对我讲的一切。”邓布利多有点尖锐地说，“我想你甚至可以相信我比你更理解。我很高兴你能告诉我，但让我向你保证，你没有说到令我不安的事情。”

sentences.text: “是的，哈利，感谢上天赐予我非凡的智力，我理解你对我讲的一切。
sentences.translation: Yes, Harry, thank God for giving me extraordinary intelligence, I understand everything you told me.
sentences.explanation: The sentence uses formal language to express gratitude and understanding towards Harry. The structure is straightforward with common vocabulary, but it showcases the use of possessive particles and modifiers in Chinese.

words.definition: particle used to form a modifier

sentences.text: ”邓布利多有点尖锐地说，“我想你甚至可以相信我比你更理解。
sentences.translation: Dumbledore said sharply, "I think you can even trust me more than yourself."
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese places the adverbial particle '地' after the adjective '尖锐' to modify the verb '说'. The phrase '甚至可以' means 'even can,' emphasizing the possibility of trusting Dumbledore more than oneself.

sentences.text: 我很高兴你能告诉我，但让我向你保证，你没有说到令我不安的事情。
sentences.translation: I am glad you could tell me, but let me assure you, you did not mention anything that makes me uneasy.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of the particle '的' to indicate an attribute in the phrase '令我不安的事情' (anything that makes me uneasy).
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important for indicating the structure and tone of the text.

content.raw_text: 哈利坐在那儿瞪着邓布利多，心里像开了锅。这到底是怎么回事？难道邓布利多真的授意过斯内普去探明马尔福的动向，他已从斯内普口中听过哈利所说的情况？还是他实际上很担忧，只是装出一副若无其事的样子？

sentences.text: 哈利坐在那儿瞪着邓布利多，心里像开了锅。
sentences.translation: Harry sat there staring at Dumbledore, feeling like his mind was in chaos.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '心里像开了锅' is an idiomatic expression in Chinese, meaning feeling like one's mind is in chaos or turmoil.

sentences.text: 这到底是怎么回事？
sentences.translation: What on earth is going on?
sentences.explanation: The phrase '到底' adds emphasis to the question, similar to 'on earth' in English. '回事' is a common phrase used to inquire about what is happening or what the matter is.

sentences.text: 难道邓布利多真的授意过斯内普去探明马尔福的动向，他已从斯内普口中听过哈利所说的情况？
sentences.translation: Could it be that Dumbledore really instructed Snape to find out Malfoy's movements, and he has heard from Snape about what Harry said?
sentences.explanation: This sentence involves complex grammar structures like the use of '过' to indicate completion of an action, as well as the possessive particle '的' to show possession. It also includes indirect speech and the use of '从...口中' to indicate hearing something from someone.

sentences.text: 还是他实际上很担忧，只是装出一副若无其事的样子？
sentences.translation: Is he actually very worried, just pretending to be nonchalant?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a question formed by using '还是' (is it that) at the beginning. The phrase '只是' (just) is used to indicate the contrast between the character's actual feelings and the appearance they are showing.

content.raw_text: “那么，先生——”哈利用他希望是礼貌、平静的声音说道，“你还是信任——”

sentences.text: “那么，先生——
sentences.translation: So, sir——
sentences.explanation: The use of '那么' at the beginning of the sentence adds a sense of transition or continuation. The term '先生' is a polite way to address a man, similar to 'sir' in English.

sentences.text: ”哈利用他希望是礼貌，平静的声音说道，“你还是信任——
sentences.translation: Harry used his hopefully polite and calm voice to say, "Do you still trust...
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a polite form of speech using the word "希望" (hope) and the structure "还是" (still) to indicate a question about trust.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks to note in Chinese text.

content.raw_text: “我已经够宽容地回答了这个问题，”邓布利多说，但语气不再宽容，“我的回答没有变。”

sentences.text: “我已经够宽容地回答了这个问题，”邓布利多说，但语气不再宽容，“我的回答没有变。
sentences.translation: I have answered this question with enough tolerance,
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases the use of the particle '了' to indicate the completion of an action, the structure of '不再' to express 'no longer,' and the repetition of the word '宽容' (tolerant) for emphasis.
The sentence contains a quotation mark and an ellipsis, which are important punctuation marks to note in Chinese text.

content.raw_text: “我想也没有。”一个讥讽的声音说。菲尼亚斯·奈杰勒斯显然只是假装睡着了。邓布利多没有理他。

sentences.translation: I don't think so.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Adverb + Negation, which is different from English. The use of "也" (also) emphasizes the negation in this context.

sentences.text: ”一个讥讽的声音说。
sentences.translation: A mocking voice said.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Adjective + Possessive Particle + Noun + Verb. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate that the mocking is related to the voice.

sentences.text: 菲尼亚斯·奈杰勒斯显然只是假装睡着了。
sentences.translation: Phineas Nigellus obviously just pretended to be asleep.
sentences.explanation: The structure '只是' is used to emphasize that the action is merely pretending. The particle '了' indicates the completion of the action of pretending to be asleep.

sentences.text: 邓布利多没有理他。
sentences.translation: Dumbledore ignored him.
sentences.explanation: The structure '没有理' means 'ignore' or 'pay no attention to' in this context.

content.raw_text: “现在，哈利，我必须坚持继续上课。今晚我有更重要的事要跟你讨论。”

sentences.text: “现在，哈利，我必须坚持继续上课。
sentences.translation: Now, Harry, I must insist on continuing the lesson.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is straightforward, but the use of '坚持' (insist on) might be a new vocabulary term for intermediate learners.

sentences.text: 今晚我有更重要的事要跟你讨论。
sentences.translation: Tonight I have more important things to discuss with you.
sentences.explanation: The structure '有...要...' is used to express 'have ... to...' in Chinese.

sentences.translation: The memory of chaos.
sentences.explanation: The sentence consists of three words: 混沌 (chaos), 的 (of), and 记忆 (memory). 的 is a possessive particle in Chinese, indicating that 混沌 belongs to 记忆.

content.raw_text: 哈利不服气地坐在那儿，如果他拒绝转换话题呢，如果他坚持争论马尔福的问题呢？邓布利多摇了摇头，仿佛看透了哈利的心思。

sentences.text: 哈利不服气地坐在那儿，如果他拒绝转换话题呢，如果他坚持争论马尔福的问题呢？
sentences.translation: Harry sat there unwillingly, what if he refused to change the topic, what if he insisted on arguing about Malfoy's issue?
sentences.explanation: The sentence presents hypothetical scenarios using '如果' (if) and '呢' (modal particle indicating a question).

sentences.text: 邓布利多摇了摇头，仿佛看透了哈利的心思。
sentences.translation: Dumbledore shook his head, as if he saw through Harry's thoughts.
sentences.explanation: The structure '仿佛...看透了' means 'as if...saw through', indicating Dumbledore seemed to understand Harry's thoughts.

content.raw_text: “啊，哈利，这是多么常见的事情，即使在最好的朋友之间！我们都相信自己要说的比对方的重要得多！”

sentences.text: “啊，哈利，这是多么常见的事情，即使在最好的朋友之间！
sentences.translation: Ah, Harry, this is such a common thing, even among the best of friends!
sentences.explanation: The structure '即使在...之间' means 'even among...' and can be a bit tricky for learners to understand at first.

sentences.text: 我们都相信自己要说的比对方的重要得多！
sentences.translation: We all believe that what we have to say is much more important than what the other party has to say!
sentences.explanation: The structure '比...的重要得多' is a common way to express 'much more important than' in Chinese.

content.raw_text: “我不认为你要说的不重要，先生。”哈利语气生硬地说。

sentences.text: “我不认为你要说的不重要，先生。
sentences.translation: I don't think what you want to say is unimportant, sir.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不认为' means 'do not think/believe'. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or association.

sentences.text: ”哈利语气生硬地说。
sentences.translation: Harry said stiffly.
sentences.explanation: The adverbial particle '地' is used to indicate the manner in which Harry said something, emphasizing the stiffness or rigidity in his tone.

content.raw_text: “嗯，你说对了，它很重要。”邓布利多轻快地说，“我今晚要给你看两个回忆，它们都来之不易，我想第二个是我收集到的所有回忆中最重要的一个。”

sentences.text: “嗯，你说对了，它很重要。
